cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code executes JavaScript with user-controlled data (target, known_targets) that flows into a web page context, but CWE-79 typically requires server-side generation serving to other users, while this appears to be client-side DOM manipulation

connection.evidence: target and known_targets parameters flow directly from set_footnote_data method parameters -> JSON serialization -> JavaScript execution -> calibre_extract.show_footnote function call

diff_causality.evidence: This is an added line that introduces JavaScript execution with user data. Reverting would remove the entire JavaScript execution pathway

security_control.evidence: No validation or sanitization of target/known_targets before JSON serialization and JavaScript execution
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-79 requires neutralization of user input before web page generation to prevent script injection
existing_controls_checked: Conditional execution based on data presence
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No encoding, validation, or sanitization applied to target/known_targets before they reach JavaScript execution context

concrete_impact.evidence: Impact depends on calibre_extract.show_footnote implementation and whether it writes user data to DOM unsafely. Direct XSS not demonstrated

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the JavaScript execution with user-controlled data would not occur, eliminating the potential injection pathway
supporting_evidence: User-controlled target and known_targets parameters flow directly into JavaScript execution
No input validation or sanitization visible in the code path
Data flows from Python to JavaScript execution context
contradicting_evidence: CWE-79 typically involves server-side generation serving to other users, while this appears to be client-side DOM manipulation (more aligned with CWE-79's DOM-based XSS variant)
The exact impact depends on calibre_extract.show_footnote implementation, which is not visible
unresolved_facts: Implementation of calibre_extract.show_footnote function and how it handles user data
Whether this JavaScript execution occurs in a security-sensitive context serving content to other users
Source and trust level of target/known_targets parameters
Whether py_bridge.footnote_data() has any security controls
review_comment: The added JavaScript execution receives user-controlled target and known_targets parameters without validation. While the data flows through JSON serialization, the calibre_extract.show_footnote function may unsafely incorporate this data into the DOM. Validate and sanitize target and known_targets parameters before JSON serialization, or ensure calibre_extract.show_footnote properly encodes output for the DOM context.
